{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[File:Philippe Biane Oberwolfach 2005.jpg|thumb|Biane at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2005]]
'''Philippe Biane''' (born 1962) is a French [[mathematician]] known for his contributions in [[probability theory]] and [[group representation]]. He was awarded the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 1995, together with [[Yuval Peres]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/award.html |title=Prize Winners 1976-2010 |access-date=2016-05-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111220062731/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/award.html |archive-date=2011-12-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Together with Marc Yor he studied the [[Brownian motion and Riemann zeta function|connections between the Brownian motion and Riemann zeta function]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Philippe Biane and Marc Yor |title=Valeurs principales associées aux temps locaux browniens |journal=Bulletin de Science Mathématique |volume=111 |year=1987 |pages=23–101 |language=fr}}</ref>
